notes.text: Settings > Motion: new "Show splash screen on startup" toggle brings back the GodotHub logo intro when the app opens. It is off by default (#382)
Projects: a project whose folder is unavailable now has a "Set new location" button, so you can point it at the folder it moved to instead of removing it and re-adding it

Remove, delete and uninstall dialogs for projects and Godot versions now have a "Don't ask again" checkbox that skips only that one dialog. Settings > Advanced lists the skipped dialogs so you can turn each one back on

Settings > Behavior: new "Code editor" field sets which program "Open in IDE" starts (for example the path to Zed), with a Browse button. Leave it empty to keep auto-detecting VS Code, Rider, IntelliJ, VSCodium and Zed (#387)

Settings > Advanced: "Check for updates on startup" is now a toggle. Turn it off and GodotHub never contacts the update server on its own; use the Check for Updates button when you want to look. It is on by default, and the first-run setup asks about it too
Workspaces: you can now choose from 92 icons instead of 12. The icon picker has a search box and category filters (General, Work, Tech, Creative, Nature, Travel and Fun)
Workspaces: a workspace can now be any color. Next to the presets there is a Custom color button that opens the same color picker the theme settings use, with a color wheel and a hex field
Windows: the GodotHub system tray icon now actually appears. Was Bugged after changing from tauri to flutter

Linux: the window position is now restored on X11 (and whenever the desktop reports it). The window manager used to ignore the position set before the window appeared, so it opened at the corner and saved that over the real position (#384)

Linux: when "Close on project open" and "Minimize to tray" are on but your desktop has no tray (for example GNOME without the AppIndicator extension), GodotHub no longer hides with no way to bring it back
Linux: running projects whose folder path contains a space are now detected correctly, so they show as running and can be stopped
Linux: a window that was maximized when you closed GodotHub now comes back with its normal size and position intact, instead of growing a little each time with the OS title bar on
Linux: the current-version command is now named godot (lowercase), so typing godot in a terminal works. Before, it was named Godot, which Linux treats as a different name
Linux: saving a bug report now uses your real Downloads folder, even if you moved or renamed it, instead of always creating a Downloads folder in your home directory

Versions: a Godot version download no longer looks stuck at 100% for a long time in debug builds, and a slow or unresponsive checksum server can no longer hold the install up forever (the check now gives up after 20 seconds and installs anyway)
Projects: the "No version selected" chip no longer overflows the project card in narrow windows. Its text now shortens with "…" when there is not enough room
Linux: the .deb and .rpm packages now recommend xdg-utils, gdbus and pkexec/polkit, which GodotHub uses to open links, detect the system tray and install updates

UI polish pass: the Dashboard stat cards and activity bars are now flat in your accent color instead of fixed blue, violet, green and amber gradients, the Versions "Open" button is smaller, the Git sidebar's Push, Pull and Fetch buttons show text labels, and the Appearance Reset button and the System language entry use proper icons instead of a heart and an emoji

Consistent text across the app: labels and buttons now use sentence case ("Save changes" instead of "Save Changes"), loading and placeholder text uses "…" instead of "...", and the title bar and task tray follow the same text sizes as the rest of the app

Create and edit workspace dialogs are wider, with the icon and color pickers side by side. The edit dialog keeps Save disabled until you change something, shows "Unsaved changes" and has a Reset button

Icons across the app are now bold, solid shapes in one consistent style (including new settings, tags, console and bug icons), and every icon plays a short animation when you hover it or the button around it. The animations follow the Motion settings

known_issues: Linux: Launching GodotHub in display scale other than 100% may cause the app to appear alot bigger than it should be. This is a known issue with Flutter and I would fixe as soon as it gets fixed upstream. (Tauri had AppImage issues and flutter has this.. ffs i am tired of making apps for linux 😭)
